design.text: Multipart, multicenter study with a 4-week placebo run-in, followed by a 4-week double-blind, placebo-controlled treatment period in which 730 subjects were randomized 1:1:1 to aprocitentan 12.5 mg, 25 mg, or placebo (Part 1); a 32-week single-blind period on aprocitentan 25 mg (Part 2); and a double-blind randomized-withdrawal period to aprocitentan 25 mg or placebo (Part 3).

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥2% and more frequent than placebo) were edema/fluid retention (9.1% vs 2.1% placebo) and anemia (3.7% vs 0% placebo) during the 4-week double-blind Part 1. A hemoglobin decrease >2 g/dL from baseline occurred in 7% of patients vs 1% of placebo. ERAs, including TRYVIO, carry risks of hepatotoxicity, fluid retention, hemoglobin decrease, and decreased sperm counts.

detail.text: WARNING: EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY — TRYVIO can cause major birth defects if used by pregnant patients and is contraindicated in pregnancy. Exclude pregnancy prior to initiation, monthly during treatment, and for one month after stopping; use acceptable contraception; available only through the TRYVIO REMS.

summary.text: TRYVIO received traditional (standard) approval via a standard-review NDA (217686). The Agency accepts blood pressure lowering as a validated surrogate endpoint and basis for traditional approval of antihypertensive agents; efficacy was shown in the Phase 3 PRECISION study. Because of the risk of embryo-fetal toxicity, aprocitentan is available only through a restricted distribution program under a REMS, and a postmarketing requirement for a descriptive study of pregnancy outcomes was mandated.

requirement.text: 4600-1 Conduct a worldwide descriptive study that collects prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to Tryvio (aprocitentan) during pregnancy and/or lactation to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications, adverse effects on the developing fetus and neonate, and adverse effects on the infant. Infant outcomes will be assessed through at least the first year of life. The minimum number of patients will be specified in the protocol.
